title: A child hidden by a timeline gives up its space in a stack
body: A `stack` lays out every child, including one a timeline hides until later. In section 11 of `figures/sufr-build.acre` a code block sits below bullets that have not appeared yet, with a gap above it. Layout happens once and a timeline changes only drawing, so the proposal needs a decision: either a stack reflows over time, or a node opts out of layout until it shows.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/0c799e42
notes.text: Jack accepted on 2026-11-23, provisionally: a node opts out of layout until it shows, rather than a stack that reflows over time.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/0c799e42
notes.text:
Built in 03ebbdd as `space shown` on the child, for example `text b11c { ...; space shown; }`.

What happens when the node shows: layout still runs once with every child in its slot. Until the node's first `show` or `fade NAME in`, the children after it draw back by its size along the stack plus the gap. As that action starts, they jump to their slots and stay there. A later `hide` does not give the space back.

Rejected: leaving the node out of layout for good and drawing it in its slot when it shows. In section 11 of `figures/sufr-build.acre` the code block would close up under `b11b`, and `b11c` and `b11d` would then draw over it. A scratch copy of that file with `space shown` on `b11c` and `b11d` draws the code under `b11b` at 256s and under `b11c` at 266s.

Rejected: sliding the later children with a `fade in` span. During the slide they cross the slot the node fades in at, and the two overlap. Tried in a demo, `figures/space-shown.acre`.

Limits: a node placed with `at` from a child after it stays at that child's slot. The stack's box, for an `auto` canvas or a scale's anchor, is the full layout. The node needs a name, sits directly in a stack, and its first change of opacity is a `show` or `fade NAME in`. Otherwise the build fails with an error.
